cards.english: Good night, sweet dreams!
Small children love sweets.
She often cooks at home.
The blue sea looks wonderful.
The old window looks very beautiful.
What a wonderful letter!
What a quiet, wonderful morning!
I am reading an interesting book.
The engineer always plays chess.
cards.existing: `Каждый` (every) and `весь` (all/whole) act like adjectives – match gender, number, case. `Каждый день` (m, nom), `всю ночь` (f, acc).

cards.english: Let's drink to your health!
cards.existing: For 'whose?', ask `чей/чья/чьё/чьи?` – same gender/number agreement: `чей это дом?` (whose house is this?).

cards.english: Sister is cooking lunch in the kitchen.
Many tourists come here in summer.
I live in a big city.
An old tree grows near the river.
The taxi took us to the hotel.

cards.target: Она едет на работу на автобусе.
cards.english: She goes to work by bus.
cards.existing: Add prefixes for more nuance: `при-` (arrive), `у-` (leave), `пере-` (cross), `до-` (reach). `Прихожу домой` (I arrive home), `ухожу` (I leave).

cards.target: Он любит свою жену и детей.
cards.english: He loves his wife and children.
cards.existing: First and second person can use either: `я люблю мою/свою жену` are both fine. Third person almost always needs `свой` (svoy) for clarity.

cards.target: Старые друзья встретились после долгой разлуки.
cards.english: Old friends met after a long separation.

cards.target: Дедушка ездил на работу на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: Grandfather went to work last week.

cards.target: Сестра готовила обед дома на прошлой неделе.
cards.english: Sister cooked lunch at home last week.
Take care of yourself and get some rest.
cards.existing: `Себя` (oneself) refers back to the subject – any person, any gender. Same form regardless: `я знаю себя` (I know myself), `он знает себя` (he knows himself).

cards.english: The salesman sometimes cleans the apartment.
It's half past nine–time to go.
An important decision needs to be made today.
cards.existing: `Должен/должна/должно/должны` (must/should) does agree with the subject in gender/number: `Я должен идти` (m), `она должна идти` (f).

cards.english: A new play is being shown at the theater.
We live on the fifth floor.
Good luck on your exam tomorrow!
A happy mother hugs her child.
cards.existing: `Свой` (one's own) refers back to the subject, regardless of person. `Он любит свою жену` (he loves his [own] wife). Use `свой` when subject = owner.

cards.english: The girl dances at her ballet lesson.
I didn't manage to buy a gift.
An interesting exhibition opened at the museum.
A short skirt is in fashion now.

cards.target: Новая книга очень важна для меня.
cards.english: A new book is very important to me.

cards.target: Сильный дождь идёт уже два часа.
cards.english: Heavy rain has been falling for two hours.

cards.target: Мама сейчас помогает другу в парке.
cards.english: Mom is helping a friend in the park right now.

cards.target: Папа сейчас помогает другу на вокзале.
cards.english: Dad is helping a friend at the train station right now.

cards.target: Мы строим каменную стену вокруг дома.
cards.english: We are building a stone wall around the house.

cards.target: Садитесь за стол, обед уже готов.
cards.english: Sit down at the table, lunch is already ready.
The engineer rarely listens to music.
The boy always helps his friend.

cards.target: Мы начинали эту работу много раз.
cards.english: We have started this work many times.

cards.target: Эта куртка стоит пять тысяч рублей.
cards.english: This jacket costs five thousand roubles.

cards.target: Новые студенты пришли в наш класс.
cards.english: New students came to our class.

cards.target: Она рисует портреты в свободное время.
cards.english: She draws portraits in her free time.

cards.target: Сестра рисует красивые картины каждый день.
cards.english: My sister paints beautiful pictures every day.
cards.existing: Frequency adverbs `всегда` (always), `никогда` (never) don't change shape. They sit before the verb: `я всегда читаю`.

cards.target: Папа ведёт машину через весь город.
cards.english: Dad drives the car through the entire city.

cards.target: Продавец часто покупает продукты в магазине.
cards.english: The salesman often buys groceries in the store.

cards.target: Мы перевезли мебель на новую квартиру.
cards.english: We transported the furniture to the new apartment.

cards.target: Бабушка вяжет тёплую шапку для внучки.
cards.english: Grandmother is knitting a warm hat for her granddaughter.

cards.target: Мнение учителя очень важно для учеников.
cards.english: The teacher's opinion is very important for the students.
The writer always helps his friend.

cards.target: Дождь идёт уже третий день подряд.
cards.english: It has been raining for the third day in a row.
cards.existing: Walking vs vehicle: `идти (idti)/ходить` for on foot, `ехать/ездить` for any vehicle. Russian distinguishes how you move, English doesn't.

cards.target: В нашем городе проживает пятьсот тысяч человек.
cards.english: Five hundred thousand people live in our city.

cards.target: Зимой мы всегда пьём чай с мёдом.
cards.english: We always drink tea with honey in winter.
cards.existing: Professions in instrumental: `работаю учителем` (rabotayu uchitelem) (I work as a teacher). When you 'become' or 'be' something in professional sense, use instrumental.

cards.target: Суп должен ещё час потомиться на огне.
cards.english: The soup needs to simmer for another hour.
cards.existing: Negative obligation: `не надо` (don't need) vs `нельзя` (forbidden). Big difference: `не надо` = it's unnecessary, `нельзя` = it's not allowed.

cards.target: Простите за опоздание, автобус задержался из-за пробки.
cards.english: Sorry for being late, the bus was delayed because of traffic.

cards.target: Мы отъехали от города на сто километров.
cards.english: We drove a hundred kilometers from the city.

cards.target: Точильщик затачивал тупые ножи на рыночной площади.
cards.english: The knife grinder sharpened blunt knives in the market square.

cards.target: Директор танцует вальс на вечеринке после обеда.
cards.english: The director dances a waltz at the party after lunch.
The postman delivers letters every day.
cards.existing: `Никогда не` (Nikogda ne) – Russian doubles up on negatives. `Я никогда не был там` (I never not have-been there). Don't drop the `не`; it's required.
